questions.q: Why do you still see `var` used heavily in existing ServiceNow server-side scripts?
options: var is faster to execute than let or const
ServiceNow's scripting engine was built for years on Rhino, an older JavaScript engine that never supported let or const
let and const are not valid JavaScript syntax
ServiceNow forbids let and const by platform policy
questions.explain: Rhino predates let/const. Modern GraalVM-based instances support both, but a lot of existing code was written for Rhino and still uses var.

questions.q: What does `typeof null` actually return in JavaScript?
questions.explain: This is a long-standing quirk of the language — typeof null returns "object", not "null". Compare directly with === null to detect it reliably.

questions.q: A variable is declared but never given a value, like `var resolvedAt;`. What is `typeof resolvedAt`?
questions.explain: A declared-but-unassigned variable holds the value undefined, and typeof correctly reports it as "undefined" — unlike the null quirk.
